Adjusted interpretation with SLOOS: The March 20 FOMC statement is modestly positive on growth and employment, with inflation easing but still elevated and policy on hold at 5.25–5.50% while QT continues. However, the latest Senior Loan Officer Opinion Survey points to ongoing credit headwinds: large banks report weaker demand for C&I loans and tighter standards for CRE (including office), foreign banks also tightened CRE standards, and consumer credit remains tighter (e.g., auto and credit cards). Residential mortgage credit is mixed—GSE-eligible largely unchanged while non-QM and other non-GSE categories tightened. Banks cite the economic outlook, risk tolerance, and liquidity/capital positions among reasons for tightening, while monitoring delinquencies and charge-offs. These SLOOS readings suggest constrained credit supply and softer loan demand could weigh on spending and investment, tempering the otherwise solid macro backdrop. Combined with vulnerabilities flagged in the Financial Stability Report (valuation pressures, office CRE, MMF structure, leveraged Treasury basis trades, rate volatility, public debt, geopolitics), the balance of risks supports a cautious policy stance and reduces the net positivity of the statement.
